2. This writ petition is filed to issue a writ of Habeas Corpus directing the respondents to produce the detenu, Bodasu Kalyan @ Kalyan Yadav S/o late Venkatesh, now detained in Central Prison,
Cherlapally, Medchal - Malkajgiri District, and to order for his release forthwith by setting aside the detention order passed by respondent No.2 vide proceedings No.26/PD-CELL/CCRB/RCKD/2023,
dated 17.04.2023 and the consequential confirmation order passed by respondent No.1 vide G.O.Rt.No.795, dated 29.05.2023.

Mr. Pothamshetti Manoj Kumar, learned counsel for the petitioner, would contend that the detaining authority has taken the crimes of 'law and order' into consideration and concluded that they are affecting the 'public order', which is illegal.

The detaining authority relied on the aforesaid three (03) crimes for passing the detention order, but the allegations levelled against the detenu in the said crimes affect the specific individual and not the public at larger.
i) He would further submit that the detention order was passed without application of mind and subjective satisfaction.
Preventive detention of a person is an extreme measure resorted to by the State when ordinary criminal law is found not adequate to control his activities which cause disturbance to public order.
In the case on hand, there is no disturbance caused to public order and the alleged offences are between the individuals.

Thus, passing of order of detention by respondent No.2 and the consequential confirmation KL,J & PSS,J passed by respondent No.1 is illegal and the same are liable to be set aside.
7.

On the other hand, learned Special Government Pleader appearing on behalf of the respondents would contend that the Detaining Authority having satisfied with the material available on record and considering the nature of offence and the manner in which it was committed by the detenu,
passed the order of detention.
He would further submit that the detenu was involved in the aforesaid crimes.
The offences committed by the detenu are grave in nature.
The Detaining Authority considering that there is every possibility of the detenu committing similar offences in future, which would again certainly affect the public order, issued detention order.
There is no error in it.
8. The aforesaid facts would reveal that the Court below dismissed fourth bail application filed by the detenu in Crime Nos.119 of 2023 and 120 of 2023.
However, the Investigating Officers on completion of investigation laid charge sheets and Calendar Cases are pending.

Apart from the aforesaid three (03) crimes/cases relied on by the detaining authority, in three (03) more Smt. Bodusu Priyanka vs The State Of Telangana on 11 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/72411676/
3 crimes/cases, the KL,J & PSS,J Investigating Officers on completion of investigation laid charge sheet against the detenu and the said cases are pending.

sentences.text: In PRC No.63 of 2022 (arising out of Crime No.538 of 2022 of Naredmet Police Station), the Court below dismissed bail applications filed by the detenu.

9. In C.C. No.913 of 2016 (arising out of Crime No.587 of 2015) and ST/SC No.206 of 2020 (arising out of Crime No.349 of 2020), the Courts below convicted the detenu and the appeals preferred by him are pending before the learned Sessions Court and this Court respectively.
10. Perusal of record would also reveal that the police have already opened rowdy sheet against the detenu and the same is pending.

The detenu did not challenge the said rowdy-sheet and it is continuing as on today.
11.

During hearing, Mr. Mujib Kumar Sadasivuni, learned Special Government Pleader, brought to the notice of this Court about registration of a case in Crime No.644 of 2023 by Kushaiguda Police Station against the detenu and others on the complaint lodged by the Jailor, Central Prison,
Cherlapally.
He has also produced copy of the KL,J & PSS,J said FIR.
The offences alleged against the detenu are punishable under Sections - 353 and 506 read with 34 of IPC and Section - 3 of the Prevention of Damage to Public Property Act, 1984.

sentences.text: The allegations levelled against the detenu are that on 02.06.2023 when the Jailor of the Central Prison along with other Officers conducting the daily admission round in the Hospital Block of the said prison, the detenu along with other convicts argued and beat the male nurse, namely Balraju.
When the Jailor and other Officers on duty tried to sort out the issue, the detenu along with other convicts retorted aggressively, threatened them and tried to beat them.
Some of the convicts of the said jail also came forward alleging that their co- prisoners are troubling them, they proceeded to swallow nails.
When the jailor along with his staff stopped them, they have also attacked them.
They have also damaged the property and frequently resorting to extortion tactics by inflicting self-hard.
12. The aforesaid facts would reveal that though the detenu convicted in the crimes registered in 2015 and 2020, he repeated similar acts in 2022.
The offences alleged against the detenu are grave and serious in nature.
Crime No.538 of 2022 was registered against the detenu alleging that he attempted to commit murder.

He KL,J & PSS,J was convicted for the offences punishable under Sections - 324 read with 34 of IPC in C.C. No.913 of 2016 (arising out of Crime No.587 of 2015) and Sections - 452, 354B, 506 and 509 and Section - 3 (2)(va) of the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Amendment Act, 2015 in ST/SC No.206 of 2020 (arising out of Crime No.349 of 2020), and the appeals are pending.

sentences.text: Even then, there is no change in the attitude and behaviour of the detenu.
Therefore, the police, Neredmet Police Station have opened rowdy-sheet against the detenu and it is continuing.
13. It is apt to note that even in Jail, the detenu committed the aforesaid offences.
The allegations levelled against the detenu are serious in nature.
Thus, the detenu is a habitual offender under the category of 'Goonda'.

Section - 2 (g) of the Act No.1 of Act, 1986 defines "Goonda", which means a person, who either by himself or as a member of or leader of a gang, habitually commits, or attempts to commit or abets the commission of offences punishable under Chapter XVI or Chapter XVII or Smt. sentences.text: The Apex Court and this Court time and again held that the detention orders shall be passed in rarest of rare cases and to prevent KL,J & PSS,J the detenu from committing similar offences which may disturb the public order.

The detaining authority while invoking the powers under the Act No.1 of 1986, has to consider the entire material on record and come to a subjective satisfaction that due to the acts committed by the detenu, nature of offences and the manner in which the same were committed would disturb the public order.
To prevent the detenu from committing the similar offences, the detaining authority shall issue preventive detention order against the detenu.

15. As held by the Apex Court, personal liberty of the citizen which the law so sedulously and carefully protects can also be taken away by the procedure established by law, when it is used to jeopardize public good and not merely private interests.
As such, it cannot be said that preventive detention issued as an instrument to keep a person in perpetual custody, without trial.
Order of detention is clearly a preventive measure and devised to afford protection to the society.
When the preventive detention is aimed to protect the safety and security of the nation, balance has to be struck between liberty of an individual and the needs of the society.
KL,J & PSS,J 16.
True distinction between 'public order' and 'law and order' was one of degree and extent of the reach of the act in question upon society.
Acts similar in nature, but committed in different contexts and circumstances might cause different reactions.
In one case, it might affect the problem of the breach of law and order and in another the breach of public order.

The power of detention having been permitted to the State under the Constitution as an exceptional power, its exercise had to be scrutinized with extreme care and could not be used as a convenient substitute for the normal processes of the criminal law of the Country.
17. It is also opt to refer that the essential concept of preventive detention is not to punish him for something he has done, but to prevent him from doing it.

The basis of detention is the satisfaction of the executive for a reasonable probability of the likelihood of the detenu acting in a manner similar to his past acts and preventing him by detention from doing the same.
Conviction in criminal case is for an act already done which can only be possible by a trial and legal evidence.
There is no parallel between prosecution in the Court of law and the detention order under the Act.
One is punitive action and the other is preventive act.

In one case, a person is punished to prove KL,J & PSS,J his guilt and the standard is proof beyond reasonable doubt, whereas in preventive detention, a man is prevented from doing something which it is necessary for reasons mentioned in the Act No.1 of 1986.
The power of preventive detention is qualitatively different from punitive detention.
The power of preventive detention is a precautionary power exercised in reasonable anticipation.
It may or may not relate to an offence.
It does not overlap with prosecution.
Even if it relies on certain facts for which prosecution may be launched or may have been launched.
An order of preventive detention may be made before or during prosecution.
An order of preventive detention may be made with or without prosecution and in anticipation or after discharge or even after acquittal.

The pendency of prosecution is no bar to an order of preventive detention and an order of preventive Smt. Bodusu Priyanka vs The State Of Telangana on 11 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/72411676/
5 detention is also not a bar to the prosecution.

sentences.text: The said principal was also laid down by the Apex Court in a catena of decisions.
18. In the light of the aforesaid legal proposition, coming to the facts of the case on hand, as discussed above, the detenu is a 'habitual offender'.
Despite convictions, he indulged in the very same offences.
There is no change in his attitude and behaviour.
Even in Jail, he has KL,J & PSS,J committed the aforesaid offences.
Police have already opened rowdy- sheet against the detenu and the same is continuing.
Therefore, according to this Court, the detenu is a 'habitual offender'.

Considering the said facts only, the detaining authority issued the impugned detention order and the same was confirmed by respondent No.1.
19.

In the light of the aforesaid discussion, in our considered view that there is no irregularity in the detention order passed by respondent No.2 and the consequential confirmation order passed by respondent No.1.
The petitioner failed to make out any ground to interfere with the said orders.
Thus, this writ petition fails and the same is liable to be dismissed.
20. The present writ petition is accordingly dismissed.
In the circumstances of the cases, there shall be no order as to costs.
As a sequel, the miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending in the writ petition shall stand closed.
